chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Irving Mills and the Swing Six records
summary: Morehouse says Mills was a businessman; Hutto joins and notes Morehouse's Swing Six records for Mills labels and Mills publishing his compositions.

bands.name: Chauncey Morehouse and the Swing Six

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: No, all right. A very important person in jazz was a man who was not a musician so much but he did a lot of show, he put together a lot of bands, Irving Mills.
You did some work for him too.
You did some recording sessions. What do you remember about Irving Mills? He was primarily a businessman.
And do you remember anything about the kinds of show, the recording sessions he put together or anything like that?
Okay. I should note for the record, Ed Hutto has joined us. Ed is an afficianado and a scholar of Chauncey Morehouse and other jazz musicians. So any time you want to chime in here, please feel free.
I guess you may cover it later but the recordings Chauncey made a few years later were for Irving Mills labels, the Master label.
Which was issued under the Brunswick and the Variety label.
Under different names, different group names?
Well Chauncey Morehouse and the Swing Six.
And I think maybe some of Chauncey's compositions that may have been published were probably published by Mills.
